status: Bounded native Legal record slice is implemented and tested over PostgreSQL, owner-local HTTP and Next transport: contract/document register and detail reads, authored document versions, hold create/request-release/release, immutable access history and the archive transition. Commercial package/release admission and the shared composition mount remain required, so the five Legal workflows are partial and no browser verification is claimed.

scope.reads: Native register (kind/search/state/page/mine, state counts, enabled, permission flags) and detail (item subtype data, documents, events, members, holds, links, comments, envelopes/signers, shares when legal.share is present, submissions, access history). Company, exact branch/department, classification membership and legal_requester own-draft visibility match the retained SQL policy. Detail records one legal_access_events record.read row in the same serializable transaction.
scope.commands: Native legal.document (draft authored version, SHA-256 checksum, UTF-8 bytes, next version, expected item version), legal.hold.create (hold + direct target + recursive target expansion + legal_hold_notices + Collaboration notifier port), legal.hold.request-release, legal.hold.release (release_requested state and independent same-person review) and the legal.transition archive path. Every command uses the existing instruction: replay before payload/source validation, enabled/editor/frozen checks, item FOR UPDATE, version CAS, legal_events, receipt, audit_events and outbox_events in one serializable unit. Hold release fails closed when the IAM same-person port is absent.
scope.http: Owner-local GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/legal/records, GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/legal/records/{id} and POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/legal/commands. Exact registered Host/Holding target, exact HTTPS Origin on commands, Idempotency-Key validation (8..180 safe characters), 512 KiB bounded JSON, private/no-store and no-referrer responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The service hashes the exact raw command bytes and passes request_hash to the backend so idempotency matches the transport body. The service returns the resolved rendered context alongside data; the PostgreSQL-backed test exercises the exact mounted handler functions without adding a tower dependency or a second axum edge.
scope.nextTransport: packages/feature-legal/src/adapters/server/native-legal.ts validates ERPX_NATIVE_LEGAL_RECORDS_CONFIG (loopback only, no reserved ports, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs/ids), forwards the actual session cookie, Host, Origin, rendered-context and branch/department selectors, and strictly validates every register/detail/command field, context identity and response bound. The retained legal API route serves native list/detail and the selected document/hold/archive commands only when the environment config exists; an invalid configuration or configured failure maps to a bounded ApiError and never falls back. SSR list composition replaces items/total/page/counts/enabled with native data while retaining the Legal shell (permissions, people, work context and purchases); record SSR detail remains retained.

behavior.authorization: legal.read is required before any register/detail query. legal.edit is required for authored document versions and archive; legal.hold for hold create/request-release; legal.hold.release for release. Editor membership is required for document/archive. Confidential/restricted records require explicit membership. legal_requester sees only its own requests. Branch/department filters are exact, matching the retained visibility SQL.
behavior.versions: Every command requires expectedVersion and re-checks it under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. Document versions use the next item-local version under the same lock. A changed version returns LEGAL_VERSION_CONFLICT before effects.
behavior.idempotency: The command receipt is checked before payload validation and source visibility. Same key + same exact request hash returns the retained result; a different hash returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The command transaction also re-checks the receipt under the company advisory lock.
behavior.holds: Hold creation preserves direct and recursively linked targets, writes Legal-owned notices, and requires a Collaboration notification port before commit. Release requires release_requested, forbids the creator and release requester (via IAM same-person), and leaves released holds immutable through the existing trigger. A notifier failure rolls back hold, notice, item version, receipt, audit and outbox rows.
behavior.archive: Archive is the native transition to archived and uses the retained allowedTransitions table, including contract overrides. Approved contracts cannot jump to archived; expired/rejected/cancelled/terminated records can. The transition increments item version and writes the event.
behavior.access: Detail insertion into legal_access_events is immutable by the existing trigger. Holds whose source record is not visible to the actor mask their reason as 'Protected by a related legal hold' while preserving direct/related state.
behavior.transactions: All reads and commands run in the existing serializable PgUnitOfWork. Commands take the legal:{company} and legal-files advisory locks. No schema, migration, root Cargo or lockfile change was made.

required: Mount erpx_server_legal::public::legal_records::legal_router in src/composition with one LegalHttpTarget per registered Holding. The target backend must resolve the normal Account session, current assignment/revision/company/branch/department and IAM permissions, construct LegalRecordsActor, and supply a LegalRenderedContext matching the resolved selection.

read must call read_legal_register/read_legal_detail on the Holding write pool and return LegalRegisterReply/LegalDetailReply. command must call execute_legal_command with LegalHttpCommandRequest.request_hash (the service already hashes the exact raw body bytes), the parsed CommandKey and the request Value, and return LegalCommandReply.

Supply Arc<dyn LegalIdentity> for same-person release review (the IAM iam_same_person projection or its public owner port) and Arc<dyn LegalHoldNotifier> for the Collaboration staff_notification effect. Hold creation fails closed without the notifier; release fails closed without the identity port.

Commercial package and Legal release admission remains a composition responsibility. The retained TypeScript command path uses withLegalPurchasedCommand/legalReadScope; this Rust slice enforces owner authorization only. Do not mount the native routes/commands as a replacement until the backend applies the current package/release admission in the same or an explicitly ordered owner unit.

Set ERPX_NATIVE_LEGAL_RECORDS_CONFIG to a private loopback origin and exact Holding targets. The Next route and SSR list use it only when present; a configured failure is returned without the retained fallback.

No PostgreSQL schema change is required. No Cargo dependency or lockfile change is required; server-legal already owns runtime/shared/sqlx/serde/sha2 and the HTTP service uses server-runtime's existing http_support re-exports. The package Cargo.toml only gains the legal_records_postgres test target.
Remove the retained TypeScript list/detail/selected-command branches only after the composition mount, purchase/release admission, browser acceptance and a consumer inventory prove no remaining user.
